governance.note: neiso-47 = the neiso-43 keeper recipe (measured Algonquin/EIA-MA-citygate DAILY gas-hub basis overlay + dual-fuel oil re-attribution + EIA-930-pinned hydro budget with 2024 plant-capacity backfill + biomass/OTHER measured must-run + historic CAMPD outage overlay + dual-limb temperature-correlated reliability floor + floor-class outage exemption + post-solve ORDC scarcity-price overlay with ISO-NE-grounded parameters) PLUS two coupled offer-side changes derived from the named month/hour-level C3b-2024 causes: (1) tranche_startup_amortization — fast-start tranche pricing (ISO-NE Market Rule 1 / FERC Order 825 analogue): the fast-start-eligible tranches (CT_PEAKER/CT_CHP econ+peak; the CC duct/quick-response peak band) carry the existing NREL start cost (fleet.BIN_STARTUP_COST_PER_MW, NREL/SR-5500-55433) exactly as the committed anchor does, amortized over each tranche's own P0 run lengths — the fuel-price-INVARIANT commitment-cost component of the real offer stack; CC econ blocks are excluded (block-loading a committed CC is not a fast start; its start costs settle as NCPC uplift, not in the LMP). No new constants. (2) the CC_REGULAR econ HR band re-anchored from the generic inherited 1.06->1.27 to 1.00->1.15 — rule #1 second-step offer-curve level calibration with the level derived from the directly-observable winter marginal implied heat rate (~8.2 MMBtu/MWh on the model's marginal winter plant, Salem Harbor base 7.38 -> mid-band ~1.08), documented in the isolation probes neiso-44/45/46 registered on the dashboard. Every lever anchors to a measured physical input, engineering data, or market-design parameter; no adder/haircut/sigmoid is tuned to a price or volume residual; the LP is not pinned to observed CEMS generation or any measured outcome; outage availability derives from historic CAMPD unit-level forced-outage windows (exogenous to net-load calibration).
governance.validation_note: Reproducible from the committed bundle: scripts/run_calibration_full.py --iso NEISO --year 2023 2024 2025 --commitment --reliability-floor --hydro-backfill-year 2024 --hydro-eia930-monthly --gas-hub-basis-daily --scarcity-price-overlay --tranche-startup-amortization --out-dir results/calibration/neiso47_faststart. Probe chain: neiso-44 (base control, keeper recipe on current main: 2024 C3b 0.160 FAIL), neiso-45 (econ flatten 0.95->1.05 alone: 2024 C3b 0.132 but C3a 2023 -6.2% — the winter over-shoot was netting a broad under-shoot), neiso-46 (fast-start v1, markup on ALL gas tranches: C3a recovers but the CC-econ markup re-inflates the mild-winter bulk, 2024 C3b 0.1518), neiso-47 (v2: scoped markup + 1.00->1.15 band: C3b 0.130/0.143/0.054, C3a -4.6/-2.3/+1.8%, all PASS). Storage throughput responds endogenously 0.74 -> 1.05 TWh (2025) with no storage-formulation change.

exceptions.metric: C2 gas family grid-delivered TWh (preliminary 2025 vintage)
exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (EIA-930 gas-vs-OTHER fold-in + preliminary-vintage incompleteness)
exceptions.reason: 2025 is a preliminary EIA-923 vintage — per-class actuals are incomplete (audit 2026-07-04: 13/30 prior CC_REGULAR plants missing, 57% reporting; gas family incomplete). The scorer falls back to the EIA-930 grid gas cell, which INCLUDES geothermal+biomass (~5.2 TWh); the correction formula under-corrects because the preliminary vintage's per-class cells are incomplete. Same categorization issue documented for the complete-vintage years, where the per-class C1 gate PASSES under the load-scaled band. When the full 2025 vintage reconciles, the per-class gate replaces this family fallback. NOT closable by adjusting model dispatch.

exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (winter fuel-inventory scarcity rent / reserve scarcity)
exceptions.reason: The energy-only LP caps the cold-hour price at the dual-fuel oil-parity (~$258/MWh). The post-solve ORDC scarcity overlay (ISO-NE-grounded LOLP curve: VOLL $2000 = Tariff III.1.10.1A offer cap, MCL 1200 MW ~ Millstone 3, sigma 900 MW = PAF Study 2022) fires and modifies econ_prices for capacity economics but does not change the persisted LP prices. The fast-start tranche pricing added in this run lifts the summer-evening and shoulder peak pricing but cannot produce >$300 cold-snap hours — that scarcity rent is the finite winter fuel INVENTORY the LP prices as an unlimited flow. Closable only via the documented winter fuel-inventory / seasonal-reliability build (docs/multi-iso/neiso-winter-fuel-inventory-plan-2026-07.md), NEVER via an offer adder tuned to the tail.

exceptions.magnitude: model 1.05 vs actual 2.08 TWh (-49.3%; was -64.6% on the neiso-44 base control)
exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (downstream of the price_tail / winter-scarcity item)
exceptions.reason: PS arbitrage throughput tracks the intraday price spread. The fast-start tranche pricing + econ-band re-anchor recovered a third of the gap ENDOGENOUSLY (0.74 -> 1.05 TWh, no storage-formulation change — per the neiso-ps-undercycling diagnosis, the PS number may only move downstream of price structure). The residual under-cycle is winter-concentrated: the LP's cold-month spread stays compressed at the dual-fuel oil-parity cap, and the real Northfield fleet additionally cycles near-daily for reserves/regulation the energy-only LP does not remunerate. Closes with the winter fuel-inventory build and/or in-LP reserve co-optimization value reaching storage; never via a storage knob.

exceptions.metric: C1 CT_PEAKER grid-delivered volume (canonical documented limitation; PASSES the load-scaled band)
exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (documentation; non-gating under the 2026-07-02 band)
exceptions.reason: NEISO's oil/gas peakers run a handful of scarcity/reserve-deployment hours the energy-only LP cannot see; the grid-delivered actual is itself near the measurement floor. Kept as the canonical NEISO ledgered limitation for continuity even though the loosened C1 band no longer gates it.
